methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 66 OCRC patients (Stage II-III) with multiplex immunofluorescence quantification of CD4+, CD8+, CD68+ cells at invasive front and tumor center. Standardized image analysis with validated methodology (90% accuracy threshold met). Statistics include Mann-Whitney U tests, Kaplan-Meier analysis, univariate/multivariate Cox regression. However, single-center design, moderate sample size, and retrospective nature limit generalizability. Authors acknowledge technical constraints in multiplex immunofluorescence and limited immune profiling scope.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study investigating tumor immune microenvironment as prognostic marker in OCRC, a clinical context with poor outcomes. Identifies immune infiltration at invasive front as independent prognostic factor with stronger predictive value than conventional clinicopathological features (HR 30.8 vs 12.7). Direct clinical relevance for risk stratification and potential therapeutic targeting.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods thoroughly describe multiplex immunofluorescence protocol, image analysis software, and statistical procedures. Results clearly presented with representative images, quantitative analyses, and survival curves. Discussion transparently addresses technical limitations of multiplex immunofluorescence and small sample size. However, no explicit adherence to observational reporting standard (STROBE), and limited data availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: First comprehensive multiplex immunofluorescence analysis of TILs and TAMs in OCRC, filling documented gap as prior literature focused on conventional CRC. Novel finding that invasive front immune infiltration shows 4-9 fold higher density than tumor center and strong independent prognostic significance. However, immune-oncology principles in CRC well-established; contribution is application to specific obstructed subtype.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear clinical context establishing OCRC as understudied population. Methods section comprehensively describes complex multiplex immunofluorescence and image analysis protocols. Results logically presented with survival analyses and clinicopathological correlations. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings against prior CRC literature and acknowledges technical constraints. Clear presentation of complex immunological data.

key_strengths: First comprehensive multiplex immunofluorescence assessment of TILs and TAMs in OCRC, addressing clinical knowledge gap in poorly prognosticated obstructed colorectal cancer population
Robust spatial analysis identifying 4-9 fold higher immune infiltration at invasive front vs tumor center, supporting 'cold tumor' phenotype hypothesis specific to OCRC

Total immune cell density (TICD) as independent prognostic factor (HR 30.8, p<0.001) exceeds conventional prognostic markers (lymphatic invasion HR 12.7), providing novel biomarker for risk stratification
Transparent acknowledgment of technical limitations (signal overlap, marker constraints) and honest discussion of small sample size with single-center design
key_concerns: Moderate sample size (n=66) with single-center retrospective design limits generalizability to OCRC populations; no multi-center validation
Technical constraints of multiplex immunofluorescence limit immune profiling to 6 markers; inability to assess T-cell phenotypes (regulatory, exhausted) or macrophage polarization (M1/M2)
No prospective validation of proposed prognostic thresholds; observed high HRs (30.8) may reflect model instability with small sample
Exploratory findings regarding SEMS vs TDT decompression device impact on immune infiltration underpowered (p=0.18 for TICD-high proportion)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective cohort study with genuine clinical novelty for understudied OCRC population using advanced multiplex immunofluorescence methodology. Identifies novel prognostic biomarker but limited by single-center retrospective design and moderate sample. Suitable for Tier 3 oncology journals (e.g., International Journal of Colorectal Disease, Cancers) with minor revisions emphasizing need for multi-center prospective validation.
